text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALES - Egypt bought a total of 600,000 tonnes of French, Australian and Argentinian wheat over the weekend. The Egyptian state's General Authority for Supply Commodities said it was buying 150,000 tonnes of French soft red wheat for January delivery, 250,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat for December-January delivery and 200,000 tonnes of Australian standard soft white wheat for December.
SOYBEAN SALE - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans at a basis over January futures on the CBOT, a company official said.

CORN TENDER - South Africa's Western Cape Buyers Association said on Monday it planned to import 250,000 tonnes of yellow maize this season and next. Due to a shortage of yellow corn this season, caused by excessive exports, the group said it had decided to invite tenders for the delivery of 30,000 tonnes of maize in February, 40,000 in March and 60,000 in April. The April consignment has been contracted.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC was tendering on November 20 for up to 16,910 tonnes of U.S. number two hard red winter wheat for export to Mozambique. Shipment was slated for Dec 5-31.

- The CCC said it was tendering on November 20 for up to 16,100 tonnes of U.S. wheat for export to Iraq. Shipment was slated for December 5-30. It sought number two or better wheat, excluding unclassed, mixed and durum wheat.

RICE TENDER - Jamaica is tendering on November 18 for 2,500 tonnes of U.S. bulk brown rice under the GSM-102 program, agents for the buyer said. The rice can be offered FOB U.S. Gulf for December 1-20 delivery or cost and freight Montego Bay, December 21-27 delivery, the agent said.

MARKET TALK - Turkey may delay its wheat import intention because local wheat prices have begun falling after recent wheat sales in the local market by the grain board TMO, officials and traders said. "The import plan will be implemented if there is a need for it. The TMO has the right to import up to 500,000 tonnes and it will resort to this when needed," a senior agriculture ministry official said.

... Egypt bought 600,000 tonnes of wheat over the weekend from countries other than the United States, a move that suggested U.S. prices were out of line with world markets, European grain traders said.

MARKET TALK (cont.) - The United States can little afford to expand its export wheat sales this year in the face of tight U.S. stocks and big exportable supplies from Europe, Australia and Argentina, U.S. exporters and analysts said.
